A `style:` directive whose property CSS doesn't know does nothing, often because of a typo. The known properties are those of the `known-css-properties` package that eslint-plugin-svelte uses. Custom properties (`style:--gap`) and properties with a vendor prefix are always fine, the latter unless `ignorePrefixed` is `false`.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-unknown-style-directive-property": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<div style:colour="red">Saved</div>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<div style:color="red" style:--gap="1rem">Saved</div>
```

## Options

| Option             | Default | What it does                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ignoreProperties` | none    | Properties to allow. A string like `"/^my-/"` is a regular expression, any other the whole name |
| `ignorePrefixed`   | `true`  | Allow every property with a vendor prefix, like `-webkit-line-clamp`                            |

Not reported with `{ "ignoreProperties": ["/^app-/"] }`:

{/* good {"options": [{"ignoreProperties": ["/^app-/"]}]} */}

```svelte
<div style:app-accent="red">Saved</div>
```
